chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The two parties in a sale have the option [to cancel] until they separate, and the owner of the animal has the option for three days.'

key_terms.الْخِيَار: The option/right to choose to cancel or confirm

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cancelling a sale in Islam before the parties separate?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt, codifies the principle of 'khiyar al-majlis' (option of the session), ensuring transactional freedom and preventing hasty commitments in Islamic commercial law. It specifically extends a three-day inspection period for livestock, reflecting the practical needs of pre-modern agrarian societies where animals required time to assess for hidden defects ('ayb'). This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on fairness and transparency in trade, rooted in the Prophet's teachings as transmitted by Imam al-Sadiq.
